title: Commercial vs. Home Loan Rates Compared
summary: Blog article comparing commercial mortgage rates with residential mortgage rates. According to the search tool's summary of the article [b], its thesis is that commercial rates tend to sit above residential ones and vary more from deal to deal; the credit spread is set case by case, and the gap is attributed to differences in risk, funding costs and exit routes. The search results attribute related guidance to sibling Silver Oak pages rather than to this article: lenders weigh the sponsor's track record, the loan-to-value ratio, the strength of the lease and the business's financials, whereas residential lending relies mainly on the borrower's income (attributed to /commercial-mortgages/); typical commercial LTV of 65% to 75% (attributed to /commercial-mortgages/); mixed-use rates usually slightly above standard buy-to-let rates but below pure commercial rates, with mixed-use LTVs typically capped at 70-75% (attributed to /faq/ and /mixed-use-property-finance/). No numeric rate figures, no H1, meta description, author, date, CTA or FAQ text from the article itself were revealed. Search (a) with the exact URL failed to retrieve the page and returned only unrelated third-party results, which are ignored.
